newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas up amid demand, Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas up amid demand, Taiwan.

text.p: Gasoline prices extended their gains on stronger bids while sellers remained on the sidelines, traders said on Wednesday.
"Sellers could be holding back for higher prices with crude firming, but fundamentaly the market is also tight, especially for first-half February," a trader said.
Sentiment was also boosted by the emergence of Taiwan for April 1-15 reformate import requirements.
The Taiwanese tender, which seeks a cargo of both leaded and unleaded 95-octane reformate, closes on March 4 and is valid for two days.

In its last tender, Taiwan bought two unleaded cargoes at $27.90 and $28.20 per barrel c-and-f, for March 16-30 delivery, respectively from a Dutch trader and a South Korean refiner. The prices registered a record in recent years.
Vietnam was also seeking spot March cargoes of 83-octane 0.15 gram per litre gasoline but had not finalised its requirements, sources told Reuters.
It had bought five 17,000-tonne Russian cargoes in its first quarter tender at 50 cents per barrel over Singapore naphtha spot quotes from Daxin, Mitsui and Trafigura.
Traders said Vietnam was seeking the spot cargoes as supplies from Russia were tight.
In the Singapore fob market, unleaded 95-octane gasoline lifting in March was bid by a Japanese shosha at $27.40 per barrel, up 30 cents from Tuesday's level.

Thailand's state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand awarded its export tender for three 30,000-barrel cargoes of natural gas liquids (NGL) for March lifting to a Japanese trader at around a discount of $1.00 per barrel to Singapore naphtha spot quotes, fob Sri Racha, sources said.
The tender closed on February 24.
